decisions: Keep the Lighthouse simulated mobile threshold and throttling unchanged; the repository gate uses simulated LCP, while the LCP breakdown table reports observed trace phases.
Reject and revert temporary content-visibility and font-display optional experiments because they did not produce a repeatable gate pass.
Treat URL-blocked JavaScript and CSS Lighthouse results as diagnostics only; these variants broke runtime or design styling and are not product fixes.
resources_used: Next.js official Server and Client Components documentation: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components
risks: The strict simulated mobile LCP gate remains unmet on all 12 portfolio routes.
Observed unthrottled local LCP is not representative proof for the simulated mobile gate or field users.
Reducing or deferring Next/React client runtime may affect navigation, mobile menu, contact form, analytics, or approved motion; validate these before accepting an optimization.
open_questions: What design-preserving change can reduce first-load hydration/runtime work enough to clear the simulated LCP gate across all routes?
Would a static HTML architecture for marketing pages be acceptable if the contact action remains a separate server endpoint?
next_instructions: Read docs/evidence/perf-lcp-investigation.md for the raw metric discrepancy and all probe results.
Do not mark G3 performance passed until a clean 3-run Lighthouse matrix proves every mobile route has LCP strictly below 2500ms.
Pursue a concrete client-runtime reduction or static-site architecture experiment without changing threshold, mobile throttling, or approved design.
